goal: Add a mechanism for fuzz targets to declare 'reachability goals' (specific code paths reached) and detect at shutdown if the current corpus stopped exercising them.
Lets a future CI job catch silent loss of fuzz coverage on high-value paths like IBD/non-IBD message handling, P2P handshakes, package acceptance, and compact block reconstruction.

result.summary: This PR adds a 'reachability goal' mechanism to the fuzzing utilities: fuzz targets register named goals identified by source location, mark them observed while processing inputs, and the process reports at shutdown which goals were never reached. Setting FUZZ_ENFORCE_REACHABILITY=1 makes the process fail if a registered goal is unmet, intended for a nightly CI job that replays static qa-assets corpora to catch silent loss of coverage. The PR instruments several existing fuzz targets (process_message(s), p2p_handshake, p2p_transport_serialization, package_eval, tx_pool, cmpctblock, partially_downloaded_block, policy_estimator_io, validation_load_mempool, utxo_snapshot) with goals for their highest-value code paths.
result.problem: Fuzz corpora can silently stop exercising important code paths (e.g. a corpus regression or upstream change) without anyone noticing, since a fuzz target that no longer reaches a valuable branch still 'passes'. This affects contributors and reviewers who rely on the fuzz corpus to catch regressions in consensus, mempool, and p2p code.

open_concerns: dergoegge and Crypt-iQ explored whether goals could be extended with richer comparison primitives (ReachabilityGoalGt etc.) or reused by other fuzzers/tools (AFL++ IJON, Antithesis); treated as future follow-up, not blocking.
maflcko suggested validation_load_mempool's goal should check specific features (txs, unbroadcast set, fee deltas) rather than plain load success; not yet implemented.
Crypt-iQ questioned buffering to std::cerr and use of std::_Exit vs std::exit in the destructor; maflcko replied explaining intent (2026-09-17) but no author follow-up push since.
resolved_concerns: Lazy goal registration causing early returns to hide unregistered goals: resolved by switching to an explicit two-phase register/observe protocol (HowHsu, 2026-08-31).
Doxygen comment style and Mutex+annotation nits from maflcko were addressed in later pushes.
Incorrect process_messages goal condition (mempool sequence assertion direction) was fixed after maflcko pointed out the inverted logic.

result.card: This PR adds a reachability-goal tracking utility for fuzz targets: targets register named goals and mark them observed per input, and the process reports/optionally fails at shutdown if a goal was never reached across the replayed corpus. It solves the problem of fuzz corpora silently losing coverage of high-value paths (IBD/non-IBD message handling, P2P handshake completion, compact block reconstruction, package/tx acceptance) without anyone noticing, intended to back a future nightly CI job replaying qa-assets. Evidence of importance: extensive engaged review from maflcko (approved), dergoegge, and Crypt-iQ debating design generality, plus concept ACKs from brunoerg and nervana21; no objections raised. It is a follow-up to merged PR #35482 and depends on it. Currently ready to review, though the CI integration that would realize its value is not yet built, and a few open design questions (exit semantics, per-feature granularity) remain unaddressed since the author's last push 17 days ago.
